findings.source_quote: ἢ θεοὺς τοὺς οὐκ ὄντας εἶναι
findings.english_quote: thinking that gods who do not exist do exist
findings.issue: The existential rendering is defensible, but the notes do not disclose the alternative predicative construction: considering those who are not gods to be gods. The alternatives distinguish denying the supposed gods' existence from denying the divinity of beings treated as gods.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note preserving the alternative ‘thinking that those who are not gods are gods’ and explaining why the main text takes τοὺς οὐκ ὄντας existentially. The present main rendering need not be rejected merely because this alternative exists.

findings.source_quote: καὶ οὕτως τὴν μητέρα ἐπιγνωσθῆναι καὶ ὑπὸ θεραπείας τὴν θεότητα πληροφορηθῆναι
findings.english_quote: and thus their mother's being recognized and becoming fully convinced of the divinity through healing
findings.issue: The draft continues the mother as the subject of πληροφορηθῆναι and takes τὴν θεότητα as the content of her conviction. That is a defensible interpretation, but the note discusses only the unnamed referent of ‘divinity’. It omits the material syntactic alternative in which τὴν θεότητα is the accusative subject of the second passive infinitive: the divinity or divine power was fully confirmed through healing.
findings.suggested_revision: Expand the note to distinguish the two constructions explicitly. If retaining the main text, explain the inferred continuation of the mother as subject and the accusative of content. Preserve the alternative ‘and the divinity was fully confirmed through healing’, supported by the parallel accusative subjects of the passive infinitives. Do not identify whose divinity is meant without further support.

findings.issue: The English collapses the magnitude expressed by τοσαύτην into the degree of speed expressed by ταχεῖαν. The Greek separately characterizes the harmony as so great and swift.
findings.suggested_revision: Render the conclusion along the lines of ‘I therefore do not think that so great and swift a harmony, converging from every direction upon one intended aim, is without providence.’ This proposed wording requires fresh review before acceptance.

findings.issue: The contextual adversative rendering is defensible, but the supplied print reads ὁμῶς, not the usual adversative spelling ὅμως. The notes do not disclose this accentual and lexical feature or distinguish the adversative interpretation from the non-adversative senses ‘alike’ or ‘together’. This is not evidence of OCR corruption and does not require renewed print verification.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note retaining ὁμῶς exactly, explaining its adversative interpretation here and acknowledging the non-adversative lexical alternative. Distinguish that interpretation from any proposed normalization to ὅμως; do not silently change the supplied Greek.
